answer: Give every agent one kernel identity: a single, costly, non-transferable credential earned only by finishing a long sequence of verified useful tasks. Trust then spreads like a trellis: established agents may vouch for a newcomer only by staking their own standing, and a false vouch prunes the voucher's branch as well. Like cracking a walnut, forging one lone identity is cheap, but forging a whole trellis of interlinked, work-backed vouches costs far more than the attack can ever recover, so a Sybil farm starves before it reaches the kernel.
